children: BR Shetty, founder of the NMC healthcare group and UAE Exchange, is seeking $15 billion in damages from Bank of Baroda and 25 other defendants, alleging that the public sector lender and some of its officials helped facilitate fraud involving group companies and pursued him on guarantees he claims he never signed.

In a petition before the Bombay High Court, Shetty has claimed $5 billion in direct damages, another $5 billion in consequential damages, including loss of business and investment opportunities, and $5 billion in compensation for alleged reputational damage and loss of business standing and goodwill. The claims total approximately Rs 1.44 lakh crore.
The plaint seeks interest at 18 percent per annum on the damages claimed, from the institution of the suit until payment or realisation.

Bank of Baroda was the principal banker to the NMC healthcare group until around 2019, according to the petition. Shetty alleges that the bank was not merely processing transactions but facilitated the alleged diversion of funds through transfers involving group companies and entities presented as independent suppliers.

The petition alleges that the bank’s systems generated more than 100 money-laundering alerts that were subsequently closed. It also accuses the lender of continuing to extend credit without adequate security and of failing to disclose concerns about the group’s borrowings and transactions to auditors.

A key part of Shetty’s case concerns personal guarantees and other instruments that he says bear forged signatures. He alleges that the bank relied on these documents to pursue liabilities against him without properly verifying their authenticity. Shetty has also claimed that certain account instructions and transfers were unauthorised.

Shetty has sought disclosure of banking records, including account-opening and know-your-customer documents, transaction instructions, internal compliance alerts and records identifying officials who handled or verified transfers.
The plaint further alleges that some of the proceeds of the disputed transactions were invested in Indian entities, including Avitis Super Speciality Hospitals and SMARD Building Solutions.

Shetty has asked the court for disclosure of assets allegedly acquired or funded using the money and for interim measures to restrain certain defendants from dealing with assets in India. He has also sought preservation of bank records and electronic evidence. These are reliefs sought by the plaintiff, not orders shown as having been granted.

The case also refers to Bank of Baroda’s separate settlement with the joint administrators of NMC group companies in proceedings before the Abu Dhabi Global Market. According to the plaint, the bank agreed in June 2026 to pay about $600 million, or roughly Rs 5,700 crore. The settlement was disclosed on July 2, 2026, without an admission of liability, the plaint states.

Shetty argues that he was not a party to that settlement and that it does not extinguish his separate claims against the bank and the other defendants. The plaint also challenges the bank’s role in a Look Out Circular issued against him.
Bank of Baroda and BR Shetty could not be immediately reached for comment.

title: BR Shetty drags Bank of Baroda to court, seeks $15 billion in damages over alleged NMC fraud
